lessons.content:
# BEP-20, ERC-20, TRC-20 — three books named USDT

USDT is a **brand** of token issued on more than one chain. The letters are the same. The books are not.

By the end of this lesson you should be able to stand in front of a withdrawal screen, name the three flavours beginners actually meet, and refuse the belief that “USDT is one chain.” If you pick the wrong **network**, you can send value into a place your wallet is not watching — sometimes recoverable with expert help, often not for a beginner, occasionally gone.

## Name the flavours you will actually meet

**ERC-20 USDT** — USDT as a contract on **Ethereum**. Addresses look like `0x…`. Gas is paid in ETH. Fees can be brutal on a small stack. Confirmations can feel slow. “ERC-20 is original” is a YouTube sentence, not a reason to spend a week of local-currency value on gas.

**TRC-20 USDT** — USDT on **Tron**. Addresses often start with `T`. Fees are a different system. A BSC wallet will not show this by default. Many P2P desks love TRC-20 because it is cheap for them. Cheap for them is not “correct for your wallet.”

**BEP-20 USDT** — USDT as a contract on **BNB Smart Chain**. Addresses look like `0x…` — **the same shape as Ethereum**. Gas is BNB. This is the flavour this academy uses for practice and later for USDT tuition rails.

The 0x shape is the trap. People think “the address worked on Ethereum so it is the same money.” It is the same **text**. It is not the same **book**. Chain ID for BSC mainnet is **56**. Ethereum mainnet is 1. Wallets that speak both still keep two ledgers.

TABLE
Withdrawal network | Chain | Address look | Gas / fee reality | Explorer
ERC-20 | Ethereum | 0x… | ETH; can be expensive | Etherscan
BEP-20 / BSC | BNB Smart Chain | 0x… | BNB; usually survivable for practice | BscScan
TRC-20 | Tron | often T… | Different wallet/network entirely | Tronscan
Something else (Solana, etc.) | Other | Other shapes | Wrong wallet will not see it | That chain’s explorer
ENDTABLE

**Worked scenario.** Kelechi copies a Trust Wallet address while the app is on BNB Smart Chain. Trust Wallet is an example of a wallet app, not an endorsement. On Binance — an example of a centralised exchange — he selects USDT, network **ERC20**, because a YouTube thumbnail said “ERC20 is original.”

1. He confirms. Ethereum includes a transfer to that 0x address **on Ethereum**.
2. His Trust Wallet, still on BSC, shows 0. He thinks it failed.
3. It did not fail. It sat on another book. Recovering it means opening Ethereum on a wallet that can speak Ethereum, with ETH for gas, and understanding that this is now an Ethereum problem.
4. Panic-sending a second withdrawal “to try BEP20 as well” is how people double-lose.
5. He stops. He opens the withdrawal receipt, reads **ERC-20**, opens Etherscan, finds the tx. Only then does he plan recovery. He does not hire a Telegram agent.

DIAGRAM
Same 0x text
    |
    +--> Ethereum book (ERC-20 USDT)     [Etherscan]
    +--> BNB Smart Chain book (BEP-20 USDT) [BscScan]
    +--> (not) Tron book                 [Tronscan, usually T…]

Balances are NOT shared.
Picking a radio button is picking a notebook.
ENDDIAGRAM

## How to choose for this academy

If the destination is a BSC wallet you set up in the last course, the withdrawal network is **BNB Smart Chain / BEP-20**. Not “default.” Not “cheapest without reading.” Match the destination’s book.

Crystal Stones the project token is BEP-20 on BSC:

`0xe252FCb1Aa2E0876E9B5f3eD1e15B9b4d11A0b00`

You cannot withdraw Crystal Stones as ERC-20 from an exchange that never listed it on Ethereum. You cannot magically bridge by picking a different radio button. This academy still will not tell you to withdraw it or buy it.

Other labels you may see: “BSC,” “BNB Smart Chain,” “BEP20 (BSC).” Those are trying to name the same book. “BNB Beacon Chain (BEP2)” is an older, different system. Do not pick BEP2 because it says BEP. Read the words **Smart Chain**.

## Defaults are not your friend

Exchange UIs remember the last network, or they pick the cheapest, or they pick the most common in your country (often TRC-20 in some African P2P markets). None of those defaults can see your wallet. You can. Select every time as if the screen were blank.

NOTE
If you already sent on the wrong network, stop. Do not send a second stack. Do not give a “recovery agent” your seed. BscScan / Etherscan / Tronscan — pick the explorer **for the network you actually selected on the withdrawal receipt** — and see if the tx is real. Recovery, if possible, is a careful later step, often with a wallet that speaks that chain. The Safety course covers panic behaviour.
ENDNOTE

## Why desks push TRC-20 and YouTubers push ERC-20

P2P desks often prefer TRC-20 because their fee sheet likes it. Western thumbnails often say ERC-20 because they learned Ethereum first. Your wallet, if you set it up in the Wallets course for BSC, prefers BEP-20. Three tribes, three radios. None of them can see your screen.

Your sentence: “Destination is BSC, so USDT BEP-20, explorer BscScan, gas BNB.” If a desk cannot send that, you need a different desk or a conscious extra hop — not an accidental hop. Extra hops are how practice size dies in two books at once.

Never let a fee table pick the network for you. The cheapest wrong book is the most expensive line.

## What this lesson is for

You should treat the network radio as the most expensive control on the withdrawal page — more expensive than the fee line.

## Say this out loud

- USDT is a name on several books. BEP-20, ERC-20, and TRC-20 are not one chain.
- 0x does not mean BSC. It might be Ethereum. Match withdrawal network to the wallet’s network.
- Wrong network plus a second panic send is how losses double.
- BEP2 is not BEP-20. Smart Chain is chain ID 56. Explorer: BscScan.
- Crystal Stones is BEP-20 to verify, not a bridge experiment.

Next: the test-send ritual, written as a procedure you can run every time.

lessons.title: The test-send ritual (tiny amount, wait, then the rest)
lessons.content:
# The test-send ritual (tiny amount, wait, then the rest)

Every non-trivial withdrawal has two transactions: a **probe**, then the **rest**. People skip the probe because the fee feels like a waste. The fee is insurance.

By the end of this lesson you should be able to run the ritual without a group chat, and you should treat “I’ll send it all, I’m careful” as the sentence that empties careful people. A **test send** is a withdrawal small enough to shrug at, used to prove address, network, and asset before the amount that would hurt.

## When a test is mandatory

- first time this asset leaves this exchange
- first time this address is used
- any time you changed network, device, or wallet app
- any time the amount would hurt if it vanished
- any time a human (broker, friend, “academy wallet”) is the destination — and for academy tuition, the destination is a published academy checkout, not a chat, when that exists
- after you reinstalled a wallet, even if the words look the same

If none of those apply and you sent to this exact whitelist yesterday, you can still test. Pride is cheaper than a probe.

## Procedure

1. On the wallet, set the network to BNB Smart Chain. Copy the receive address with the copy button.
2. On the exchange, paste. Check first 6 and last 6 characters against the wallet screen — with your eyes, not with a friend in chat.
3. Select **BEP-20 / BSC** for USDT (or BNB native for BNB).
4. Send the smallest amount the platform allows, or a few dollars equivalent — an amount you can shrug at.
5. Wait. Open **BscScan**. Paste **your** address, not a hash a stranger sent. Wait for the token row (USDT) or the BNB balance change.
6. Confirm asset, network, amount, destination. Only then send the rest. Same screen, same network, same address, already checked.
7. If the test fails, stop. Do not send the rest. Do not “try a different network with the full stack.”

TABLE
Test shows | You do
BscScan token tab: USDT arrived, right address | Send the rest, still checking first 6 / last 6
Nothing on BscScan, tx on Etherscan | You picked ERC-20. Stop. Do not send the rest on a third network.
Nothing anywhere after the exchange says complete | Wait confirmations; then ticket with their tx hash
Arrived at an address you do not recognise | Paste attack. Freeze. Do not “retry.”
Wallet icon missing but BscScan has the token | UI hide; the book is fine. Do not resend.
ENDTABLE

**Worked scenario.** Yemi is withdrawing 80 USDT of practice money plus a little BNB.

1. Yemi sends 1 USDT BEP-20 first. Fee feels annoying. Yemi pays it.
2. Twelve minutes later BscScan shows 1 USDT at Yemi’s address. Wallet app shows it after a refresh.
3. Yemi sends the remaining 79 on the same network to the same address, then a small BNB native withdraw as a separate test-and-rest if the BNB size also matters.
4. If step 2 had shown zero, Yemi would still have 79. That is the whole religion.
5. A friend said “just send it, you did this last month.” Last month’s address was a different phone. The ritual does not care.

DIAGRAM
Copy address (wallet, BSC)
    |
    v
Paste + eyes on first 6 and last 6
    |
    v
Network = BEP-20 / BSC (for USDT)
    |
    v
Tiny amount --> wait --> BscScan agrees
    |
    +-- yes --> send the rest
    +-- no  --> STOP. Ticket or recover the test. Never the remainder.
ENDDIAGRAM

## Waiting is part of the ritual

Exchanges queue. Chains confirm. Wallets cache. Ten minutes of boredom is not a failed tx. Refresh BscScan, not the send button. “Still pending” on the exchange means they have not finished broadcasting. “Pending” on the explorer means the chain has the tx and has not finished burying it. Those are different pendings. Read which screen.

Do not speed things up by raising gas on a CEX withdrawal. You do not control that gas. They do.

## Fees on two sends

Two withdrawal fees are still cheaper than one funeral. If the platform’s minimum is already your whole stack, you are too small to be doing this today, or you accept that the whole stack **is** the test — which means the stack should have been practice size.

NOTE
Never ask a group to “watch the test with you” by pasting the address in public. You do not need an audience. You need BscScan. Academy staff will not confirm your test send in WhatsApp. We will also not take the rest “to keep it safe.”
ENDNOTE

## Minimums that force the test to be the stack

If the CEX minimum withdrawal is 10 USDT and you only have 10, then 10 **is** the test. That means 10 had to be practice size from the start. Do not deposit a month of rent and then discover the minimum is the whole pile.

Some platforms let you internal-transfer 1 USDT to a second account you control as a drill. That does not test the chain. Only a withdrawal tests the network radio. Do not confuse an internal move with a probe.

When the test lands, whitelist. The ritual is not finished at the explorer row. Sticky withdrawals are part of arriving.

## Overnight pending is a sleep, not a second send

If the test sits pending overnight, sleep. Morning-you can read the explorer. Overnight-you will invent a second network. Internal transfers are not probes; only a withdrawal tests the radio.

## What this lesson is for

You should be unable to hit Confirm on a full-size first withdrawal without feeling that you skipped a step.

## Say this out loud

- Tiny amount, wait, explorer agrees, then the rest.
- The test fee is insurance, not a waste.
- If the test fails, the remainder stays put. No second network with the full stack.
- Wait is part of the ritual. Refresh the explorer, not the send button.
- Last month’s successful send does not bless a new device or a new network.

Next: paste attacks and poisoned addresses — why your eyes on first 6 and last 6 are not optional.

lessons.title: Paste attacks and poisoned addresses
lessons.content:
# Paste attacks and poisoned addresses

You can pick the right network and still send to the wrong person. The clipboard is a battlefield.

By the end of this lesson you should treat every paste as hostile until your eyes check it, and you should know what **address poisoning** looks like. **Paste attack** means: malware or a “helper” replaces the address in your clipboard with theirs after you copy. **Poisoning** means: someone sends you a tiny tx from an address that looks like one you use, hoping you copy **their** address from the history.

## Clipboard malware

You copy your address from the wallet. A hidden program swaps it for an attacker address. You paste into the exchange. First 6 and last 6, if you only check those on some fonts, can be made to rhyme. So you check more than the ends, and you check against the **wallet screen**, not against the chat log of what you think you copied.

Defences:

- copy with the wallet’s button, paste once, look at the exchange field
- compare first 6 **and** last 6 **and** a chunk in the middle to the wallet screen
- a hardware wallet that shows the address on its own display is stronger; if you have one, use the screen on the device
- do not install “clipboard manager plus crypto” APKs from groups
- do not let remote-desktop “support” watch you copy

If the pasted address and the wallet disagree, assume malware. Do not send. Move the remaining IOU only after you are on a cleaner device. This is freeze-and-breathe territory from Module 2.

## Address poisoning

Your explorer history shows:

- a real incoming 50 USDT from the exchange
- a later incoming 0.001 USDT (or a fake-token “USDT”) from an address that starts and ends like the exchange’s hot wallet, or like your own other address

You later copy “the address I always use” from history, and you copy the poison. You just volunteered.

Defences:

- do not copy destination addresses from explorer history
- copy from the wallet receive screen, or from a paper whitelist you wrote
- on BscScan, a dust incoming from a lookalike is a clue to ignore that from-address forever
- hide spam tokens; do not interact

TABLE
What you copied from | Verdict
Wallet receive button, then eyes vs screen | Default
Hardware device display | Better
Exchange whitelist you added after a test | Good
BscScan history of lookalike dust | Hostile
WhatsApp “here is your address again” | Hostile
A PDF invoice from “the checkout processor support” in chat | Hostile — published checkout is not a DM
ENDTABLE

**Worked scenario.** Chika copies her BSC address, pastes into the CEX, checks first 4 characters, sends 70 USDT.

1. Last 4 also matched a lookalike the malware had prepared. The middle did not. She did not look at the middle.
2. BscScan shows the tx to an address that is not the wallet’s receive screen.
3. The chain did its job. The clipboard lied.
4. Chika stops. She does not send a second 70 “because maybe it will bounce.” It will not bounce.
5. She kills sessions, scans the phone, and treats the remaining exchange IOU as still hers — because she did not send it. Freeze is still wise if the device is dirty.

DIAGRAM
Wallet shows:  0xA1B2 ... 89CD
Clipboard may: 0xA1B2 ... 89CD   (honest)
           or  0xA1B2 ... 77EE   (swap)
           or  0xA1B2 ... 89CD   lookalike with different middle

Eyes: first 6, last 6, AND a middle chunk.
History on BscScan: not a copy source.
ENDDIAGRAM

## Chat is not a confirmation channel

“Please confirm this is my address” in WhatsApp is how people get a yes from a cloned contact. You do not need a friend to confirm your own receive screen. If you are paying someone else, you need an out-of-band check you already trust — not a like-reaction on a paste.

Academy tuition, when live, is USDT on BNB Smart Chain (BEP-20) through academy checkout through published checkout. It will not be a poisoned lookalike in a DM, and not PaynovaX.

## Contract addresses are not destinations for a first withdrawal

Withdrawing USDT to the USDT **contract** address, or to Crystal Stones’ contract `0xe252FCb1Aa2E0876E9B5f3eD1e15B9b4d11A0b00`, does not “deposit into the token.” It can burn or strand funds depending on how that contract handles incoming transfers. You withdraw to **your wallet address**, the one that holds keys. Verify a contract to identify a token. Do not treat the contract as a mailbox.

NOTE
If a paste already went wrong, the explorer is the truth. Do not chase with a recovery agent. Do not send more. Write down the tx hash. The Safety course is where panic gets a longer protocol. Today: eyes on the string, every time.
ENDNOTE

## Unicode lookalikes in the middle of 0x

Attackers can use characters that look like `0` or `l` in some fonts. Ends match, middle is a different address. If anything feels off — extra length, odd glyphs — cancel. Paste into a plain text field that shows the raw string. Hardware screens that checksum the address are better than tired eyes at midnight.

Also refuse QR codes from chats for your **own** receive address. You have a receive button. A QR from “support” is their address with your logo. Scan-to-send malware exists on phones too. Official app camera for a destination you already verified is one thing. A QR that arrived with a threat is another.

## What this lesson is for

You should be unable to confirm a withdrawal without a visual check that would catch both malware and a poisoned history copy.

## Say this out loud

- The clipboard can lie. Check first 6, last 6, and a middle chunk against the wallet screen.
- Do not copy addresses from explorer history. Poison dust exists to be copied.
- Chat confirmation of your own receive address is theatre, not security.
- Do not withdraw tokens to a contract address. Your wallet address is the mailbox.
- A wrong paste will not bounce. Do not send a second stack after it.

Next: after confirm, you believe the explorer — not the group chat.

lessons.title: After confirm: explorer, not the group chat
lessons.content:
# After confirm: explorer, not the group chat

The withdrawal button is not the finish line. The finish line is a row on the public book.

By the end of this lesson you should know which explorer to open, what to paste, which fields prove a success, and why a WhatsApp screenshot is not evidence. An **explorer** is a website that reads a chain and shows transactions, addresses, and token transfers. For BNB Smart Chain that explorer is **BscScan**.

## What to open

- BEP-20 / BSC → **BscScan**
- ERC-20 / Ethereum → Etherscan
- TRC-20 / Tron → Tronscan

If you are not sure which you picked, the exchange withdrawal receipt names the network. Believe that line, then pick the explorer that matches. Do not pick the explorer a group member likes.

Paste **your address** or **the tx hash from the exchange**. Do not paste a hash a stranger sent “to help you look it up.” Hashes can be real transfers on a different chain, a different token, or someone else’s 1 USDT.

## What success looks like on BscScan

For USDT: a **token transfer** row, contract matching the USDT BEP-20 the exchange uses, **To:** your address, amount matching what the receipt said (minus their fee, depending on how they display it). Status success. Enough confirmations that your wallet also sees it.

For BNB: a native transfer, value in BNB, to your address.

A failed on-chain tx is rare for a CEX withdrawal (they usually do not broadcast losers), but “dropped” and “replaced” exist. Read the status. Pending for a long time is wait, then ticket — not a group vote.

TABLE
You see | It means | You do
BscScan token transfer to you, right asset | It landed | Update your personal ledger; stop
Etherscan success, you wanted BSC | Wrong book | Stop; do not send again; recover later if you can
Tronscan success, wallet on BSC shows 0 | Wrong book | Same
Group screenshot of a green tick | Theatre | Ignore
“Support” hash that is a different token | Distraction | Only the receipt’s hash
ENDTABLE

**Worked scenario.** Riley’s test 1 USDT shows “completed” on the example CEX.

1. Riley copies the tx hash from the **bookmarked** withdrawal history, not from a DM.
2. Riley opens BscScan, pastes the hash. Token transfer: USDT, to Riley’s address, 1 USDT.
3. Riley also pastes the address into BscScan and sees the same row on the token tab.
4. A group admin says “I don’t see it, send again.” Riley does not. The book sees it. The admin is not a ledger.
5. Riley sends the rest only because step 2 matched. Riley does not post the hash publicly. Public hashes plus amounts are a shopping list for thieves.

DIAGRAM
Exchange: "withdrawal complete" + tx hash
        |
        v
Explorer for THAT network
        |
        +-- success, right To, right asset --> believe the book
        +-- success, wrong chain/token     --> you mis-picked; do not retry blind
        +-- nothing                        --> wait confirmations, then official ticket

Group chat is not on this diagram.
ENDDIAGRAM

## Wallets can lag; explorers less so

A wallet app might need a network switch, a pull-to-refresh, or a custom token add. BscScan already knows. If BscScan has the USDT and the app does not, add the token (the real USDT BEP-20 contract, not a lookalike) or wait. Do not withdraw again.

If you add a custom token, you are pointing the UI at a contract. Verify the contract. Crystal Stones, if you ever add it to look, is `0xe252FCb1Aa2E0876E9B5f3eD1e15B9b4d11A0b00` — looking is not buying.

## Tickets, not tributes

If the explorer of the named network shows nothing after a honest wait, open a ticket in the bookmarked app. Include hash, amount, asset, network, time. Do not pay a “priority investigator.” Do not send BNB to a “boost address.” Those are invoices.

NOTE
Academy staff will not “confirm your hash” in WhatsApp as a substitute for BscScan. If someone wearing our name wants you to send a follow-up payment to make the explorer update, they are a thief. Explorers update because miners/validators included a tx, not because you paid a mentor.
ENDNOTE

## How to read a BscScan token transfer without folklore

Open the tx. Check:

- Status: success, not dropped
- Token contract: the USDT you expect on BSC, not a spam token with the same letters
- From: the exchange hot wallet (it will not be your email)
- To: your address, matching first 6 / last 6 / middle
- Amount: the receive amount

If those five match, you are done. Comments at the bottom of BscScan are public graffiti. They often say “this is a scam, contact recovery.” That graffiti is the scam. Never message addresses from tx comments.

Save the hash in the personal ledger. Do not save it as a tweet.

## Ignore BscScan comments

The comments under a tx are public graffiti, often “contact recovery.” That graffiti is the scam. Never message those addresses. If the five fields (status, contract, from, to, amount) match, you are done. Refreshing send is not refreshing the explorer.

## What this lesson is for

You should retire the group chat as a settlement layer and replace it with the explorer of the network on the receipt.

## Say this out loud

- After confirm, the explorer of that network is the boss, not the group chat.
- Paste your address or the receipt’s hash. Never a stranger’s “helper” hash.
- Success is the right asset to the right To. A green screenshot is theatre.
- If the wallet lags and BscScan shows the token, do not withdraw again.
- Tickets live in the bookmarked app. Boost-address invoices are theft.

Next: dust, leftovers, outages, and travel-rule delays — the unglamorous ways money sits still.

lessons.title: Dust, leftovers, outages, and travel-rule delays
lessons.content:
# Dust, leftovers, outages, and travel-rule delays

Not every missing unit was stolen. Some of it is **dust**, some is a leftover IOU, some is an outage, some is law.

By the end of this lesson you should be able to name those four stalls, and you should not feed them to a recovery agent. **Dust** means: an amount so small that fees make moving it silly. **Travel rule** means: extra identity information some platforms must collect before they let a withdrawal of a certain size leave, because regulators asked.

## Dust and leftovers

After fees, you may have 0.40 USDT IOU on the exchange and 0.0002 BNB on-chain. Moving the BNB can cost more than it is worth. That is dust. Leave it, or live with it as leftover fuel if it still pays a send.

Leftovers also happen because you bought 0.01 BNB and withdrew 0.009 after a fee. The 0.001 is not missing. It is the bill, or it is below minimum withdrawal.

Do not “clean out” dust by connecting the wallet to a random sweeper site. Sweepers ask for signatures that can take the tokens that are **not** dust.

TABLE
What you see | Likely cause | Adult move
0.30 USDT IOU, min withdraw is 1 | Below minimum | Leave it or add size later; do not chase
Wallet shows 0.00015 BNB | Dust relative to gas | Leave as leftover fuel or ignore
Withdrawal pending 40 minutes, status page shows incident | Outage | Wait on their status page; no DM helpers
Withdrawal form asks who the beneficiary is | Travel-rule questionnaire | Answer honestly in the official form, or cancel; never in chat
Exchange down, Twitter says hack | Maybe, maybe rumour | Freeze assumptions; official status; do not send seeds
ENDTABLE

**Worked scenario.** Tobi withdraws most USDT, leaves 0.8 because the minimum is 1. He also has 0.001 BNB on-chain after gas.

1. He calls both “stolen by fees.” One is a min-withdraw leftover IOU. One is dust.
2. A site offers “dust aggregator — connect wallet.” He does not.
3. Next week the exchange has an outage. His remaining 0.8 is stuck as an IOU. Uncomfortable, not a chain failure.
4. When withdrawals reopen, a travel-rule popup asks for beneficiary details because he raised size. He fills it on the bookmarked site. He does not photograph the form into a group.
5. A DM says “pay 20 USDT to release travel rule.” He reports it. The popup never asked for a prepayment.

DIAGRAM
Still sitting somewhere
    |
    +-- below min withdraw --> leftover IOU
    +-- smaller than gas    --> dust
    +-- company incident    --> outage queue
    +-- extra identity form --> travel-rule delay
    +-- actually stolen     --> freeze, sessions, whitelist (Module 2)

Treat the last one as last, after you have named the first four.
ENDDIAGRAM

## Outages

Exchanges pause deposits, trades, or withdrawals. Chains can also clog; BSC is usually cheap and quick, not always. During a pause, your IOU is still their IOU. Spamming withdrawals can lock funds in “processing.” Read the status page from the bookmark, not a Twitter clone.

If the company is truly insolvent, you are a creditor. That is law, not a Telegram reverse-tx. This academy will not pretend a recovery wizard can un-insolve a firm.

## Travel-rule and compliance delays

Larger withdrawals, new devices, new addresses, and some corridors trigger questionnaires: who owns the destination wallet, what is this for, source of funds. Annoying. Expected. Fill them in the official UI. Lying is fraud. Paying a stranger to “fast-track compliance” is theft plus, sometimes, a mule story.

Weekend plus a new whitelist address plus a first-time BEP-20 USDT withdrawal is a pile of delays that can look like a hack. It is often just the pile.

## Do not donate leftovers to a stranger

“I’ll sweep your dust if you send the rest plus seed” is not a service. Neither is “send leftover USDT to this gas address.” If you want BNB, withdraw BNB. If you want the leftover IOU, wait until you are above minimum, or accept it as tuition to the fee schedule.

NOTE
Crystal Stones Academy will not collect dust, leftovers, or “listing deposits.” Paid tracks, when live, are USDT on BNB Smart Chain (BEP-20) through academy checkout at a published checkout. A travel-rule delay on your CEX is your CEX. We cannot click withdraw for you, and anyone who says they can is not us.
ENDNOTE

## When an outage meets a panic send

The pattern: withdrawals paused, group screams, someone DMs an “emergency OTC” that will take your IOU off-platform. That OTC is hunting people who cannot wait. If the IOU is practice size, you can wait. If it is not practice size, that was the earlier mistake.

Official status pages lie slowly. DMs lie fast. Prefer slow.

If travel-rule asks for the owner of the destination wallet, and the owner is you, say you. If the owner would be a cousin you are hiding, you are in a story this academy will not help you write. Cancel the withdrawal. Do not invent a beneficiary.

## What this lesson is for

You should classify a stall before you escalate, and you should keep leftover size away from sweeper sites and chat invoices.

## Say this out loud

- Dust is too small to move sanely. Leftovers are often min-withdraw or fees, not theft.
- Outages freeze IOUs. Status page, not DMs.
- Travel-rule forms belong in the official UI. They are not a 20 USDT chat invoice.
- Sweepers and gas-for-dust sites are how leftover tokens become missing tokens.
- Name the stall before you call it stolen.

Take the quiz. Last module is a lab: you will narrate a first buy and a first withdrawal without doing one, including the wrong-network failure.

lessons.title: A personal ledger is not Twitter (records you actually keep)
lessons.content:
# A personal ledger is not Twitter (records you actually keep)

If you cannot say what you paid, what you hold, and where it sits, you did not finish a first buy. You performed one.

By the end of this lesson you should have a private **personal ledger**: a written record for yourself, not a feed. **Personal ledger** means: the notes you keep of dates, venues, amounts, fees, networks, tx hashes, and which book the value sits on. It is not a Twitter thread. It is not a WhatsApp flex. It is not tax advice — we are not your tax advisor — it is how adults remember.

## What you actually write down

For each movement, at least:

- date and time (your timezone)
- venue (which CEX, which wallet app — examples, not ads)
- asset and amount
- what you paid in local currency or in USDT, all-in if you can
- network, if any chain was touched
- tx hash, if any chain was touched
- where it sits **now**: CEX IOU, or which chain at which address (first 6 / last 6 only in the notes if you are paranoid about screenshots)
- whether a test send already blessed this destination

You do not need fancy software. Paper, a local encrypted note, a spreadsheet that is not a screenshot in a group. Do not photograph this next to a seed. Do not put a seed in the ledger. An exchange login is not a seed either — do not store passwords here.

TABLE
Record | Why it exists | Wrong home for it
All-in local currency (or dollars) spent | So you cannot lie to yourself about “profit” | A group chat
Withdrawal tx hash | So a ticket has a spine | Twitter
Network used | So you do not “remember BEP-20” incorrectly | Memory
Current book (IOU vs chain) | So screens that disagree do not scare you | A mentor DM
Seed phrase | Does not belong in this ledger | Anywhere digital, period
ENDTABLE

**Worked scenario.** Riley, after the narrated evening, writes four lines in a notebook kept with household papers, not in the camera roll.

1. “12 Mar — example CEX — P2P — 30,000 local currency → 18.2 USDT IOU (seller rate 1,648; no off-platform chat).”
2. “Same day — market-bought 0.02 BNB, still IOU. Receipt fee 0.02 USDT.”
3. “Same day — test 1 USDT BEP-20, hash 0xabc… on BscScan, then remainder, then 0.02 BNB native. Address 0xA1B2…89CD. Whitelist on.”
4. “Sitting now: 0 USDT on CEX, ~17 USDT BEP-20 in wallet, ~0.019 BNB after gas. Practice. Not Crystal Stones. Stop.”

Riley does not post line 3. A hash plus an amount is a map.

DIAGRAM
Public feed (Twitter, group)
   "I'm in crypto now"   <-- not a record

Personal ledger (private)
   date, venue, amount, fee, network, hash, current book
        |
        v
You can answer "where is it?" at 2 a.m. without a stranger
ENDDIAGRAM

## What you do not record in public

Balances. Full addresses. Screenshots of 2FA. KYC photos. The anti-phishing word. A boast that you “just withdrew 500.” Thieves read. Family members who will nag you into sending to a cousin’s broker also read.

If you teach someone Riley’s checklist, teach the checklist. Do not teach your numbers.

## This is not a tax opinion

Some countries tax trades, some tax withdrawals, some ignore you until a threshold. This academy is **not a tax advisor**. A personal ledger makes a later conversation with a professional possible. A Twitter flex makes it worse. Keep receipts. We will not tell you how to file.

In Nigeria, in the UK, in the US, the forms differ. The adult habit does not: write down what moved.

## Reconciliation once, calmly

Once a week, not once a candle: does the CEX still show what you think? Does BscScan still show what you think? If not, you either forgot a fee, forgot an internal transfer, or you have a Module 2 problem. Reconciliation is how disagreement becomes a sentence instead of a panic.

NOTE
Crystal Stones Academy will never ask you to screenshot your personal ledger into mentor chat. We do not need your balances. Paid checkout, when live, is USDT on BNB Smart Chain (BEP-20) through academy checkout — you will have a payment receipt there too. Keep it private. It is not a group trophy.
ENDNOTE

## One page you could hand a professional later

Imagine a calm accountant, years later, asking what you did in 2026. Your ledger should let you say: this local currency left this bank on this day, became this USDT IOU on this venue, then this hash on BSC. That is enough for a professional to start. A folder of memes is not.

You do not need to be that accountant. You need to not destroy the trail. Do not delete exchange emails. Do not reset the app before you export order history if the platform offers export. Do not keep the only copy of the ledger on the same phone that holds the only authenticator.

If you stop using crypto after this course, the ledger still earns its keep: you can see that you did not “lose everything to the blockchain” — you paid spread, fees, and maybe one lesson-sized mistake.

## Do not title a cloud note “seed plus ledger”

The ledger can live on paper or in an encrypted local file. The seed cannot live there. Keep a second copy of the ledger somewhere that is not the only phone with the only authenticator. Export order history if the platform offers it before you delete an app.

## What this lesson is for

You should be able to answer “where is the practice stack?” from a private page, not from memory and not from a like-count.

## Say this out loud

- A personal ledger is private records: date, venue, amount, fee, network, hash, current book.
- Twitter is not a ledger. A group flex is not a receipt.
- Do not store seeds or passwords in the ledger. Do not post hashes with amounts.
- This is not tax advice. It is how you stay honest with yourself.
- Reconcile CEX and explorer calmly. Disagreement has a name.

lessons.title: When screens disagree after a withdrawal
lessons.content:
# When screens disagree after a withdrawal

Module 4 taught disagreement **before** withdraw (they should). This lesson is disagreement **after**.

By the end you should walk a diagnostic that names the book that is behind, without feeding the problem to a chat. **After** means: you clicked withdraw, the company said something, the explorer said something, the wallet said something, and they are not the same picture.

## The three screens

1. **Exchange withdrawal history** — their claim: pending, completed, failed; sometimes a tx hash.
2. **Explorer of the network on the receipt** — the chain’s claim.
3. **Wallet app** — a view of the chain, sometimes stale, sometimes on the wrong network, sometimes hiding a token.

Truth order: explorer of the named network first, then exchange, then wallet UI. The wallet is a window. Windows get dirty.

TABLE
Exchange | Explorer (right network) | Wallet | Name it
Completed + hash | Success, right To | Shows token | Done. Update personal ledger.
Completed + hash | Success, right To | 0 | UI lag / wrong network in app / token not added
Completed + hash | Success, **wrong** To | 0 | Paste attack. Stop.
Completed + hash | Empty after a real wait | 0 | Ticket with hash; do not resend
Pending, no hash | Empty | 0 | Company has not broadcast. Wait or official ticket. Not a chain issue.
Failed | Empty | 0 | IOU should have bounced back. If not, ticket.
Completed | Success on **other** explorer | 0 on BSC | Wrong network. Do not send again.
ENDTABLE

**Worked scenario.** After Riley’s rest-of-stack USDT withdraw, the CEX says complete. BscScan shows the USDT. Trust Wallet (example app) shows 0.

1. Riley does not resend. Riley checks the wallet is on BNB Smart Chain, not Ethereum.
2. Riley pulls to refresh. Still 0. Riley opens BscScan token tab: USDT is there.
3. Riley adds the token in the UI if needed, verifying the USDT BEP-20 contract — not a lookalike, not Crystal Stones by accident.
4. The wallet catches up. The personal ledger already believed BscScan.
5. If instead BscScan had been empty, Riley would wait confirmations, then open a bookmarked ticket with the hash. Riley would not ask the group to “boost.”

DIAGRAM
Withdraw clicked
    |
    v
History hash? --no--> company queue (wait / ticket)
    |
   yes
    v
Right explorer: tx to me, right asset?
    |
    +-- yes, wallet 0 --> fix the window (network, refresh, add token)
    +-- yes, wrong To --> paste attack; stop
    +-- no, other chain --> wrong network; stop
    +-- no, nowhere --> wait, then official ticket
ENDDIAGRAM

## Partial truths that feel like theft

- Withdrawal fee deducted, amount on-chain is less than you typed. Read “receive amount” on the receipt.
- Token shows as a duplicate USDT with a different contract. One is spam. Do not swap it. Hide it.
- BNB arrived, USDT did not, because you only sent BNB so far. Two withdrawals, two waits.
- Travel-rule hold: history says processing, no hash. That is Module 5, not a missing chain.

## What you say to support (and not to anyone else)

Hash, asset, amount, network, time, your user ID. No seed. No 2FA. No remote desktop. No “please withdraw for me.” If a responder asks for those, you are not in the real ticket.

Do not post the problem with your full address and remaining balance in a group. You will collect helpers.

## A worked delay that is not theft

Withdrawals also stall for boring reasons that still make screens disagree.

- The company is waiting on its own hot-wallet queue. History: processing. Explorer: empty. Wallet: 0. You wait. You do not pay a boost address.
- Travel-rule form not submitted. History: on hold. Explorer: empty. Fill the official form.
- You looked at Etherscan for a BEP-20 send. Explorer you opened: 0. Right explorer: success. Wrong window.
- Token transferred but the wallet is still on Ethereum mainnet in the network picker. Switch to BNB Smart Chain (chain ID 56), then refresh.

Write the stall in the personal ledger as a named stall, not as “hacked.” If twenty minutes later the explorer still has nothing and the receipt has a hash, then ticket. If there is no hash, it has not hit a chain. Calling it “the blockchain ate it” is the Module 3 folklore again.

If two assets were supposed to move — USDT and BNB — disagreement can be one success and one queue. Read each withdrawal row separately. Do not treat a BNB arrival as proof the USDT also moved.

NOTE
Screens after a withdrawal are allowed to lag. They are not allowed to send you to a recovery agent. Academy staff will not debug your hash in a DM as a substitute for BscScan. We will also not take the leftover IOU “to test the rail.”
ENDNOTE

## Two assets, two diagnostics

USDT can succeed while BNB is still queued, or the reverse. Run the table once per withdrawal row, not once per mood. People see BNB arrive and assume USDT “must be in there.” Token tab and native balance are different lines on BscScan.

If a spam token named USDT arrived from a poisoning address at the same time as the real USDT, the wallet might show two. Hide the spam. Do not swap it. The real one matches the contract the exchange named. Looking is allowed. Tapping Approve on a spam token is how disagreement becomes a drain.

## What this lesson is for

You should diagnose a post-withdraw mismatch in five minutes of reading screens, and only then, if needed, open an official ticket.

## Say this out loud

- After withdraw, explorer of the receipt’s network is first, exchange history second, wallet UI third.
- Wallet zero plus explorer yes is a window problem, not a resend.
- Explorer yes to the wrong To is a paste attack. Stop.
- No hash yet is a company queue, not a broken chain.
- Support gets a hash in a real ticket, never a seed, and they will not withdraw for you.

lessons.title: Moving from IOU to a wallet you control — only after Wallets course habits
lessons.content:
# Moving from IOU to a wallet you control — only after Wallets course habits

Self-custody is not a reward for clicking Buy. It is a set of habits from the Wallets course, reused here.

By the end of this lesson you should know **when** to withdraw, **what** must already be true about the destination, and **why** this academy will slow you down if those habits are missing. **Self-custody** means: keys you control can sign. If those keys are a screenshot in WhatsApp, you did not move to safety. You moved to a more honest way to get robbed.

## Prerequisites, said as a gate

Do not withdraw practice USDT to a wallet until you can say yes to:

- I can explain that the wallet does not hold coins; the chain does
- I have a seed backup that is not a photo, not a cloud note, not a group admin’s “safe keep”
- I can switch the app to BNB Smart Chain on purpose
- I can copy a receive address without typing it
- I know BNB is gas and USDT is not
- I will not connect this wallet to a DEX I am not using yet tonight
- Nobody, including academy staff, has asked for the seed — and I would refuse

If any line is no, the stack can stay as a CEX IOU of **practice size** while you go back to Wallets. Company risk is real. Seed-in-chat risk is often larger for a beginner who just got excited.

TABLE
Ready | Not ready
Paper or steel seed, offline | Seed in camera roll / email / “mentor”
Address copied from receive on BSC | Address from a group PDF
Will test-send | Will send all because fees
2FA + whitelist on the CEX | SMS 2FA, empty whitelist
Will stop after withdraw | Will connect PancakeSwap clone same hour
ENDTABLE

**Worked scenario.** Jordan finished this course’s walkthrough in his head, then installed a wallet in a hurry during a live “listing.”

1. He screenshots a 12-word phrase “just for tonight.”
2. He withdraws the whole IOU to that wallet, no test, network default TRC-20.
3. He has left a company IOU and arrived in a wallet whose seed is a photo, on the wrong chain.
4. The honest move, which he skipped, was: keep practice size on the CEX until the seed was offline, then test BEP-20, then rest, then stop.
5. This academy would rather he stay a customer of a CEX for another week than become a key-holder with a photographed seed. That is not endorsement of any CEX. It is ranking of failures.

DIAGRAM
Wallets course habits in place
        |
        v
CEX IOU of practice size
        |
        |  test BEP-20  --> explorer --> rest + BNB
        v
Address you control, seed offline, gas present
        |
        X  skip habits --> photograph seed, wrong network, DEX same night
ENDDIAGRAM

## What “a wallet you control” is not

- an exchange “web3 wallet” tab you do not have the seed for
- a broker’s address they “made for you”
- a the checkout processor address from chat (tuition, when live, is published checkout — you pay it, you do not custody it)
- Crystal Stones’ contract
- a multi-sig you do not understand yet

Control is: you can sign, you can restore from your backup, nobody else must.

## Size still matters after you withdraw

On-chain coins have no “forgot password.” Practice size remains the rule. If the number would wreck you, it is too large to learn on, whether it sits as IOU or as BEP-20.

You do not have to withdraw everything. Leaving a little IOU for fees and a later send is allowed. So is withdrawing all practice funds if the CEX is just a door. That is a preference, not a purity test. What is not allowed is withdrawing into sloppy keys.

NOTE
This academy will never ask you to move IOUs into a “shared academy wallet,” a PaynovaX account, or a Crystal Stones treasury for safekeeping. Self-custody is yours. Checkout is the checkout processor USDT BEP-20 when paid tracks exist. Two different rails. Neither is a DM.
ENDNOTE

## The hurry that skips the seed backup

The usual skip: KYC finished Friday, group is loud Friday night, wallet installed Friday night, seed photographed “temporarily,” full stack withdrawn Friday night, DEX connected Saturday because PancakeSwap — a DEX you are not using yet — had a ticker with the right letters.

Put the seed on paper **before** the first inbound test. Confirm you can restore on a second view (or at least that the paper is readable) before the rest of the stack moves. If that feels slow, good. Slow is the gate.

If you already photographed a seed, that wallet is burned for serious size. Practice dust can stay while you create a new wallet with a paper backup, then test-send to the new address. Do not “delete the photo and hope.” Photos leak from clouds you forgot you enabled.

A CEX IOU of practice size for one more week is cheaper than a burned seed with your whole experiment on it. That is ranking of risks, not an advert for leaving funds on exchanges forever.

## Paper first, inbound second

Put the seed on paper before the first inbound test. If you already photographed a seed, that wallet is burned for serious size — make a new one with paper, then test-send. A CEX IOU of practice size for one more week is cheaper than a burned seed with the whole experiment on it.

## What this lesson is for

You should treat withdrawal as a promotion you earn with Wallets habits, not as the default last step of a hyped evening.

## Say this out loud

- Self-custody starts when a withdrawal lands at an address whose keys you hold and whose seed is offline.
- If Wallets habits are missing, practice size can stay an IOU while you go back.
- A photographed seed is not safety. It is a more honest theft.
- Do not withdraw into a broker’s mailbox or a contract address.
- Size still matters on-chain. There is no forgot-password.

lessons.title: Full lab recap: speak a first-buy + first-withdrawal out loud, step by step, with the wrong-network failure included
lessons.content:
# Full lab recap: speak a first-buy + first-withdrawal out loud, step by step, with the wrong-network failure included

This is the exam you give yourself in a kitchen, not on a live book.

By the end of this lesson you should be able to speak a complete first-buy and first-withdrawal, then speak the wrong-network failure, without opening an account. If you cannot speak it, you are not ready to click it. **Lab** means: rehearsal. Not a buy order. Not a Crystal Stones allocation.

## Part A — speak the happy path

Say this, filling the blanks with your own country’s rail (P2P in local currency, or bank, or card):

1. I arrive at the exchange through a bookmark I saved on a calm day, not an ad.
2. I created the login myself. It is not a seed. I use authenticator 2FA, not SMS as the long-term lock. Anti-phishing word is on. I will whitelist after a test.
3. I fund through a parented door: in-app P2P or official bank/card. Exact name, exact amount. I do not follow WhatsApp. I do not release before the goods if I am the seller.
4. Local money becomes an IOU. I write that in a personal ledger. BscScan is still zero. It should be.
5. I market-buy a practice size of USDT if I still need it, and a little BNB on a liquid pair. Spot only. Size I can lose. I do not ape a ticker.
6. Destination: official wallet app, network BNB Smart Chain, copy receive. Eyes: first 6, last 6, middle chunk.
7. Withdrawal: asset USDT, network BEP-20 / BSC, test amount. I wait. BscScan token tab agrees. Then the rest. Then BNB native, tested if the size matters.
8. I whitelist that address. I stop for the day. I do not open a DEX I am not using yet.

If you skipped a sentence, go back. The skipped sentence is where people vanish stacks.

## Part B — speak the wrong-network failure

Now speak the failure on purpose, so your mouth knows it:

1. I copy a BSC `0x` address.
2. I leave the withdrawal network on ERC-20 or TRC-20 because it was the default, or because someone said it was cheaper.
3. The company says complete. My BSC wallet shows 0.
4. I do **not** send a second full stack on another network.
5. I read the receipt. I open the explorer **of that network**. I find the tx. I now know which book I wrote in.
6. Recovery, if any, is later, with a wallet that speaks that chain, and never with a seed sent to a helper.
7. My personal ledger records: “wrong network, test size, stopped.”

The lab is not complete until Part B is as fluent as Part A.

TABLE
Spoken line | If you cannot say it
Bookmark, not ad | You will phish yourself
IOU, not chain, after fund | You will panic at BscScan zero
BNB is fuel | You will strand USDT
Test then rest | You will donate the stack to a typo
Receipt names the network | You will double-send
Explorer, not group | You will pay a helper
Stop for the day | You will ape
ENDTABLE

**Worked scenario.** Two students rehearse out loud. Sam speaks Part A cleanly and mumbles Part B. Emeka forces both.

1. Next week Sam funds for real, skips the test, picks TRC-20, loses practice size, and says the course failed her.
2. The course asked her to speak Part B. She skipped the lab.
3. Emeka does a 1 USDT test, sees BscScan, sends the rest, still has rent.
4. Neither was told to buy Crystal Stones. Neither paid a Telegram the checkout processor. Emeka has a hash in a notebook.
5. This is the pass mark: speech first, tiny size second, silence in groups third.

DIAGRAM
LAB (kitchen, no live funds)
  Part A happy path  -->  mouth can teach Riley
  Part B wrong network --> mouth can stop a second send
        |
        v
LIVE (practice size only)
  same words, slower, with explorers

Skip lab --> live panic --> helpers
ENDDIAGRAM

## Part C — the sentences you refuse

Speak these refusals too:

- “SMS 2FA is enough.” No.
- “Support will withdraw for me.” No.
- “USDT is one chain.” No.
- “Release, I sent a PDF.” No.
- “I bought so it is in my wallet already.” No.
- “Memo is optional.” Not when the screen required it.
- “the checkout processor is a Telegram wallet.” No. USDT BEP-20, published checkout, when paid tracks exist.
- “Send Crystal Stones to this contract to join.” No. Verify `0xe252FCb1Aa2E0876E9B5f3eD1e15B9b4d11A0b00` is not a buy, not a mailbox.

NOTE
If you are speaking this lab in a classroom, use fake amounts. Do not pass phones around with live 2FA. Do not shout addresses. Rehearsal is not a funding round.
ENDNOTE

## Grade yourself with a listener

If another adult is willing, they listen without coaching. They tick a paper list: bookmark, 2FA, fund as IOU, BNB fuel, copy address, BEP-20, test, explorer, rest, whitelist, stop, wrong-network stop. Any tick they cannot hear, you do not have.

If you are alone, record a voice note you will delete, and listen once. Mumbles are skips.

Do not run the lab with live 2FA codes spoken into a room. Do not pass a phone around a classroom with an open exchange session. Rehearsal uses fake amounts and fake last-4s. Live practice, later, is solo, tiny, and quiet.

## What this lesson is for

You should be able to teach the happy path and the wrong-network stop to another adult, as speech, without opening a live book.

## Say this out loud

- I can narrate venue, fund as IOU, tiny spot BNB, test USDT on BEP-20, explorer, rest, whitelist, stop.
- I can narrate the wrong-network failure and the rule: no second full send.
- Exchange login is not a seed. Explorer is not a group admin.
- the checkout processor is not a chat wallet. Crystal Stones is not this lab’s buy.
- If I cannot speak it, I do not click it.

Next: what this course does not make you.

lessons.title: What this course does not make you (not a trader, not a tax advisor, not “ready to ape Crystal Stones”)
lessons.content:
# What this course does not make you (not a trader, not a tax advisor, not “ready to ape Crystal Stones”)

A Basic course that ends in a coronation is a funnel. This one ends in a fence.

By the end of this lesson you should be able to list what you are **not**, as clearly as what you can do. That list is the product. **Not** is not an insult. It is how you keep the practice stack.

## You are not a trader

You can describe a spot pair, a fee, a fill, and a stop rule. That is literacy. It is not a desk. You have no edge because you finished a quiz. You should not sell signals. You should not manage a cousin’s salary. You should not open futures to “make back” a P2P spread.

If you later study trading, that will be a different course with different honesty about how often beginners lose. It is not smuggled in here as a trophy.

## You are not a tax advisor, lawyer, or compliance officer

You know KYC exists, chargebacks exist, travel-rule forms exist. You do not know your filing position. Do not tell a group “P2P local currency is invisible.” Do not tell a group “BscScan is anonymous enough.” Laws attach to people. This academy will not help you hide.

## You are not “ready to ape Crystal Stones”

Crystal Stones is a BEP-20 token on BNB Smart Chain. The contract, to **verify** only, is:

`0xe252FCb1Aa2E0876E9B5f3eD1e15B9b4d11A0b00`

Verification is not a market order. Listing rumours are not a market order. A purple logo is not a market order. RWA claims are **their claim to verify**, not our instruction. This course trained rails: CEX IOU, BNB gas, BEP-20 withdrawals. Rails are not a buy.

Anyone who says “you finished Exchanges, now ape CSTN” is not this academy.

TABLE
This course made you | This course did not make you
Able to name an IOU versus on-chain coins | A profitable trader
Able to fund through a parented door | A P2P merchant with a public rate
Able to refuse SMS-only 2FA and fake support | Invincible
Able to test-send BEP-20 USDT | Ready to ape Crystal Stones
Able to say the checkout processor is USDT BEP-20 checkout | A collections agent for chat wallets
Able to keep a personal ledger | A tax advisor
ENDTABLE

**Worked scenario.** A student finishes the last quiz and lands in a Telegram that says “Academy class of today — deposit Crystal Stones to this wallet for whitelist.”

1. The student names the object: a chat wallet, not the checkout processor, not BscScan of their own address.
2. The student does not pay. The student does not argue long enough to be worn down.
3. The student can still verify the real contract later, on BscScan, without sending.
4. The student still has practice USDT and BNB, or still has an IOU, depending on whether they withdrew.
5. That refusal is the graduation, not a fill on a thin book.

DIAGRAM
What you can do
  explain CEX, KYC, 2FA, P2P, spot, BNB gas, BEP-20, test send, explorer

Fence
  no trader identity
  no tax advice
  no Crystal Stones buy order
  no chat checkout
  no seed to anyone
  no “support will withdraw for me”
ENDDIAGRAM

## What you can do tomorrow, if you choose

- Rehearse the lab out loud again
- If — and only if — you choose to practise with money you can lose, run Riley’s checklist at practice size
- Keep the personal ledger
- Go on to the BNB Smart Chain beginner course without a new ticker

You can also do nothing with money this month. Literacy does not expire overnight. FOMO does.

## Payments for this academy, said once more

When Intermediate or Advanced checkout is live, it is **the checkout processor**, paid in **USDT on BEP-20**. Not Crystal Stone token. Not PaynovaX. Not a wallet pasted in WhatsApp. Not an exchange screenshot as payment. If that sentence ever collides with a DM, the DM is fake.

NOTE
Education only. We will not tell you to buy or sell any asset, including BNB, USDT, and Crystal Stones. We will tell you that an exchange is a company, that a withdrawal is a chain write, and that the people who skip those sentences pay for everyone else’s screenshots.
ENDNOTE

## What “next course” is for

BNB Smart Chain for beginners will teach the chain those withdrawals land on: chain ID 56, BscScan more slowly, gas, tokens as contracts. Safety will teach panic, approvals, and recovery-theatre. Neither will crown you a trader. Neither will tell you to ape Crystal Stones.

If a marketer uses this certificate — when certificates exist — as a buy signal, they are lying about the fence. You can show them this lesson’s title.

You may still, independently, choose to buy or not buy any asset with money you can lose, after you can speak the lab. That choice will never be this academy’s instruction. The fence stays up even if a future you climbs it. We did not open the gate.

## Literacy is the output. A fill is optional.

You are allowed to finish this course and do nothing with live funds for a month. If a marketer treats a future certificate as proof it is time to ape Crystal Stones, they are lying about the fence. Next courses teach the chain and safety. They still will not crown a trader.

## What this lesson is for

You should leave Basic’s third course as a careful beginner with language, not as a newly minted ape with a brand.

## Say this out loud

- I am not a trader because I can click Spot. I am not a tax advisor because I know KYC exists.
- I am not ready to ape Crystal Stones. The contract is to verify, never a buy order on this page.
- the checkout processor USDT BEP-20 is published checkout, not a Telegram wallet.
- Support will not withdraw for me. An exchange login is not a seed.
- I can fund, size, test-send, and stop — or I can wait. Both are adult.

This was Exchanges & Your First Buy. Next in Basic is the chain those withdrawals land on: BNB Smart Chain for beginners.
